name: Students in grades 3 to 8 proficient in math
definition: Share of New York City public school students in grades 3 to 8 (district schools; charter schools excluded) who scored proficient, Level 3 or 4, on the New York State mathematics exam.

latest_extra.note: 286,169 tested; results released August 2026 (file as of August 3, 2026).

source.name: NYC Public Schools, citywide Math results 2018-2026 (InfoHub), and Math Test Results 2013-2023 (NYC Open Data 74kb-55u9)

method: Citywide, all grades (3-8), all students, '% Level 3+4'. 2018 onward from the InfoHub citywide workbook (sheet 'Math - All'); 2013-2017 from the DOE's Open Data file of earlier results. In overlapping years the two sources agree within 0.05 points.
caveats: No results for 2020 (tests cancelled) or 2021 (tests optional; about 21 percent of eligible students took them), per the DOE's notes.

Two breaks in comparability, per the DOE's notes: in 2018 the state shortened the tests from three days to two and rescaled them, so 2017 and earlier should not be compared directly with 2018 and later; in 2023 the state aligned the tests to new standards (Next Generation) with new scales and cut scores, so 2022 and earlier should not be compared directly with 2023 and later.
Charter school students are not included.
The state moved grades 5 and 8 to computer-based testing in 2024 and grades 4 and 6 in 2025.
Grade 7 and 8 students who take a Regents math exam instead of the grade-level test are not in the math results, which lowers the number tested.
No peer comparison: each state sets its own tests and proficiency bars.
